bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Patna protests intensify as Prashant Kishor backs students, farmers | MorungExpress
bihar_raw_news.content: (Photo: IANS) India 25th August 2026 Patna, August 25 (IANS) Patna witnessed a tense day on Tuesday as student organisations protesting recruitment and examination issues joined farmers opposing the proposed Pataliputra Greenfield Satellite Township in demonstrations across the city. Police erected barricades at several locations to prevent student protesters from marching towards Lok Bhavan. Reacting to the police action, Bankipur MLA Prashant Kishor said recent events had demonstrated the strength of democracy. He argued that authorities now appeared to think twice before using force against protesters, describing this as a positive development. Kishor urged the government to address what he termed the legitimate demands of students and farmers, saying such concerns could not simply be suppressed. He highlighted issues including alleged privatisation and commercialisation of education, the growing influence of coaching institutes, examination paper leaks, rising unemployment and dissatisfaction among youth. He warned that failing to address these concerns could lead to larger student movements in the future. When reporters told him student aspirants were looking for him, Kishor said he was already in Patna and regularly moving around the city. Alongside the student protests, farmers from Punpun, Naubatpur, Masaurhi, Fatuha and surrounding areas demonstrated against the township project. Kishor backed their concerns, alleging that the government’s land policy could benefit major industrialists at farmers' expense. He claimed valuable agricultural land could be transferred at inadequate prices, arguing that the policy was difficult to implement in Bihar and warning that attempts to acquire large areas of productive land could lead to widespread unrest. Farmers said their agricultural land was their primary source of livelihood and that they produced three crops a year. They argued that surrendering land would threaten their families’ ability to fund education, marriages and other essential expenses. Protesters demanded the government reconsider the proposed acquisition, maintaining they did not want to surrender their land. Patna District Magistrate, SSP and SP reached the protest site and held discussions with farmer representatives, attempting to persuade them to resolve the matter through dialogue. The Bihar government has proposed developing 12 townships across the state, including the Pataliputra Greenfield Satellite Township. Farmers opposing the Patna project insist their agricultural land should not be acquired for development.

bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar participates in national conference of Information and Public Relations Secretaries ANI | Updated: Aug 25, 2026 19:42 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 25 (ANI): Bihar Information and Public Relations Department Secretary Naveen Kumar represented the State at the national conference of Information and Public Relations Secretaries from States and Union Territories held at Vigyan Bhawan in the national capital on Tuesday. Senior officials from the Central Government, including the Secretary of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Chanchal Kumar, along with representatives from various States and Union Territories, attended the conference. The conference aimed to make information and public communication systems between the Centre and States more effective, adopt new mechanisms in line with the evolving media landscape and strengthen mutual coordination. Discussions were held on various policy and operational matters concerning the information and broadcasting sector, according to the release. A key focus of the conference was strengthening the partnership between the Press Information Bureau (PIB) and Information and Public Relations Departments of States and Union Territories. The meeting also discussed utilisation of training facilities at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC) for capacity building of Information and Public Relations officers. The conference also covered the framework for WAVES 2027, enhancing market access through 'WAVES Bazaar', expanding public service broadcasting infrastructure and making state-specific programmes and public outreach more effective. Deliberations also included adoption of the 'India Cine Hub' single-window portal for film shooting and live event permissions, as well as increasing state participation in public service broadcasting. The agenda further included the transition to a digital system through the 'Press Sewa Portal' under the Press and Registration of Periodicals (PRP) Act, 2023, promoting low-cost cinema in rural and underserved areas, implementing accessibility standards in cinema halls and making the 'WaveX State Ecosystem' effective. Bihar 's participation in the conference was aimed at aligning the State's information and public relations system with emerging technologies, digital media and institutional frameworks at the national level, according to the release. The conference provided a platform for the exchange of experiences and best practices, as well as for strengthening coordination and capacity building between the Centre and the states. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.content: Home · News Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced a plan to develop a 126-kilometre Marine Drive along the Ganga , with an estimated investment of ₹70,000 crore . The proposed corridor would extend the state’s riverfront road network from the Patna region towards Koilwar on the Son River. The announcement was made on August 23 during the concluding ceremony of an Employment Fair at Gyan Bhawan near Gandhi Maidan in Patna. The Chief Minister said the project is aimed at improving infrastructure while creating employment and attracting private investment. Advertisement ₹70,000 Crore Investment Proposed According to the plan outlined by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the proposed investment would be divided between the state government and the private sector. The proposed structure is: ₹20,000 crore – Bihar government contribution ₹50,000 crore – Expected private-sector investment ₹70,000 crore – Total estimated investment 126 km – Proposed length of the corridor Choudhary said the project would create new opportunities for investment and employment along the proposed route. J.P. Ganga Path to Form the Base The proposed corridor will build on the existing J.P. Ganga Path in Patna, which has become popularly known as the city’s Marine Drive. According to the Chief Minister, the existing road stretch is around 21 kilometres long . The project was initiated in 2013 and completed in 2025 at an estimated cost of around ₹6,000 crore. The new proposal would significantly expand the riverfront road network beyond Patna and connect it with a much longer stretch along the Ganga. Corridor to Connect Infrastructure and Economic Growth The government is presenting the proposed Marine Drive as more than a connectivity project. The extended corridor is expected to create opportunities for economic activity and private-sector participation. The project could support: Improved river-side road connectivity Expansion of infrastructure along the Ganga Greater private investment New employment opportunities Growth of commercial and economic activities Wider urban and regional connectivity Announcement Made at Employment Fair The project announcement came during an employment-focused programme organised by the Department of Youth, Employment and Skill Development . Offer letters were distributed to candidates selected by various employers during the event. The government linked the proposed infrastructure investment with its wider focus on employment generation and creating new economic opportunities for young people. Government and Private Sector to Share Investment The proposed financing model places a significant share of the investment on the private sector, with ₹50,000 crore expected to come from private entities. The Bihar government has proposed contributing ₹20,000 crore towards the project. The detailed financing structure, implementation mechanism and execution plan will determine how the proposal moves forward. Proposed Corridor Could Expand Bihar’s Riverfront Network If implemented, the 126-km Marine Drive would represent a major expansion of Bihar’s existing riverfront infrastructure. The proposal would take the concept of the J.P. Ganga Path beyond Patna and create a much larger corridor along the Ganga, potentially supporting connectivity, investment and employment across the region. For now, the ₹70,000-crore, 126-km Marine Drive remains a government proposal

bihar_raw_news.content: Kharge, Rahul Gandhi urge PM Modi to scrap caste census questionnaire Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi have urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to scrap the existing caste census questionnaire and formulate a new one after consulting political parties, experts and the public, citing Telangana and Bihar's caste surveys as examples. By PTI Published Date - 25 August 2026, 05:32 PM New Delhi: Leaders of Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the caste census issue, demanding that the government scrap the existing questionnaire for it and formulate a new one after consulting political parties, experts, and the general public. Kharge and Gandhi said they do not accept the caste census being conducted in the current manner and urged the government to take a cue from the caste surveys done in Telangana and Bihar. Briefing reporters on the letter written in Hindi by Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Kharge and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Gandhi on August 20, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the government’s current efforts towards a caste census are just a “whitewash”. Ramesh noted that this is the third letter written by the Congress leadership to Modi over the issue but has not received any reply. In their letter, Kharge and Gandhi said social justice policies in India cannot be effectively implemented without accurate data and a precise assessment of the numerical strength and socio-economic status of various castes is possible only if the caste enumeration is conducted correctly. “Your government has opted for an open-ended question format to record caste details in the census, which is misleading. Under this method, whatever name an individual provides for their caste will be recorded as it is,” the leaders said in their letter to Modi. In India, the same caste is known by different names, sub-castes, and linguistic variations across different regions, Congress president Kharge and former party chief Rahul Gandhi pointed out. Consequently, if members of the same caste are recorded under different names during the census, a single caste could end up being fragmented into thousands of distinct names, they argued. This would result in a list of hundreds of thousands of caste names, rendering the entire dataset obtained from the caste census useless, Kharge and Gandhi argued. “If the actual population of a community is not accurately recorded, any assessment of its status will also be flawed. bihar_raw_news.content: Rapid Fire Prev Next Bihar Raises Concerns Over Renewal of Farakka Water Treaty 25 Aug 2026 3 min read Tags: Rapid Fire CA Quick Facts For Prelims GS Paper - 2 GS Paper - 3 Source: IE The possible renewal of the 1996 India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Sharing Treaty (Farakka Treaty) , set to expire in December 2026, has triggered a debate in Bihar, with the state seeking safeguards for concerns related to flooding, siltation, and dry-season water availability. Ganga Water Sharing Treaty (Farakka Treaty): The India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Sharing Treaty was signed on 12th December 1996 between India and Bangladesh to regulate the sharing of Ganga waters at the Farakka Barrage during the dry season (1st January to 31st May). The treaty established a 30-year framework (1996–2026) for predictable water sharing and replaced earlier short-term arrangements such as the 1977 Ganga Water Agreement. It provides a formula-based mechanism for sharing Ganga waters during the lean season. Unlike the 1977 agreement, the 1996 treaty does not contain a guaranteed minimum flow clause. If the available flow falls below 50,000 cusecs, both countries are required to enter into emergency consultations. Farakka Barrage: The Farakka Barrage , located on the Ganga River in Murshidabad district, West Bengal , was constructed and operationalised in 1975. The barrage was built to divert water from the Ganga through a feeder canal into the Hooghly River to reduce silt accumulation and maintain the navigability of the Kolkata Port . Bangladesh’s Concerns: Reduced downstream flow affects water availability, soil salinity, agriculture, and ecosystems in southern Bangladesh. Bihar’s Concerns: Farakka Barrage has contributed to a “flood-and-parch” situation , with concerns over increased silt deposition, rising riverbed levels, reduced river carrying capacity, frequent monsoon flooding in districts such as Bhagalpur and Munger , and reduced dry-season water availability. Bihar has sought consideration of its projected water requirements up to 2050 , along with scientific silt management strategies and greater representation of affected states , in any future revision of the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty. Joint Rivers Commission (JRC): India and Bangladesh address shared river management issues through the Joint Rivers Commission (JRC) , established in 1972 to promote cooperation over common water resources. The commission facilitates exchange of hydrological data, discussions on transboundary river issues, and cooperation in the development and management of shared water resources . Ganga Basin Challenges: The Ganga basin faces complex river management challenges, including sedimentation, changing river dynamics due to climate variability, groundwater alterations, upstream water withdrawals, and the need for integrated basin-level management . "We have already clarified our position. Notably, in the Bihar SIR judgment, the Court had held that ECI cannot decide citizenship of a person and the conclusions reached by it (after SIR) would be relevant only for electoral purposes. bihar_raw_news.title: India's mushroom production surges, led by Bihar , but challenges remain | Agriculture
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / Industry / Agriculture / India's mushroom production surges, led by Bihar, but challenges remain India's mushroom production surges, led by Bihar, but challenges remain India's mushroom output rose from 51,000 tonnes in 2015 to 347,750 tonnes in 2024, with Bihar at the forefront, but productivity, cold-chain and infrastructure gaps threaten further growth. premium Mushroom Sanjeeb Mukherjee New Delhi 7 min read Last Updated : Aug 25 2026 | 6:46 PM IST Listen to This Article If one were to prepare a list of crops whose production has shown exponential growth over the past decade or so, mushrooms would figure prominently in such a ranking. India’s mushroom production has jumped exponentially in the nine years from 2015 to 2024, rising from a mere 51,000 tonnes to almost 347,750 tonnes and registering a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 23.76 per cent, according to country-wise records maintained by the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). In comparison, China, which remained the world’s largest producer of mushrooms of all kinds for both edible and non-edible purposes and accounted for almost 94 per cent of annual global output, registered a production CAGR of just 3.80 per cent between 2015 and 2024. During the same period, total global mushroom production rose by 3.62 per cent, while total production excluding China rose by just 1.06 per cent. India, which has a minuscule share of global mushroom production, thus recorded the fastest production growth in the past nine years. So, how was this rapid growth in mushroom production achieved? How did Bihar become India’s mushroom production leader? According to a recent paper by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), India’s ‘mushroom kranti’, or mushroom revolution, has largely been led by states such as Bihar, Odisha and Maharashtra, with Bihar at the forefront. Bihar has emerged as a leader, contributing 12.02 per cent of India’s total mushroom production in 2023-24, the paper said. Odisha follows with 9.86 per cent, while Maharashtra accounts for a 9.49 per cent share of India’s total production. The report highlighted that the Bihar government’s initiatives, such as the Bihar Agriculture Roadmap, the ‘Mushroom Kit Vitaran’ Scheme (mushroom minikit distribution programme) and Integrated Development of Horticulture, have played a crucial role in promoting mushroom cultivation in the state. In addition, institutional support from bodies such as the Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University (RPCAU) has further aided this revolution through training programmes, research and capacity-building initiatives, empowering farmers, particularly women, to adopt mushroom farming as a viable livelihood option, the ICAR paper said. Implemented as an intangible state asset, the ontology will enable the creation of multiple agents and services accessible across departments and by citizens directly, unlocking cross-department service delivery and the creation of new public service capabilities and digital value on this asset. This shared foundation can enable departments to build AI services faster and work together more seamlessly, while giving citizens simpler and more integrated access to government services. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the decade-long success of the Unified Payment Interface. It has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an inter-operable, real-time payments platform. Our correspondent reports that by bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation.

national_raw_news.title: Puducherry Govt introduces Puducherry Business Reforms Bill, 2026 4 hours ago 64
national_raw_news.content: The Government of Puducherry today introduced the Puducherry Business Reforms Bill, 2026, aimed at making the Union Territory a simpler, faster and more investment-friendly destination for businesses and entrepreneurs. The Bill seeks to shift business regulation from permission-based control to rule-based governance, with emphasis on transparency, predictability and time-bound decision-making. A major focus of the Bill is on MSMEs and entrepreneurship. It proposes to extend the exemption from approvals for MSMEs to five years, with a further one-year extension, and introduce auto-generation of Acknowledgement Certificates if they are not issued within the prescribed time. Invest Puducherry will also be strengthened as a single point of contact for investors. The Bill proposes greater flexibility in land use and development regulations, rationalisation of building and zoning requirements, and removal of duplicative and obsolete compliances. An auto-appeal mechanism is also proposed to enable applicants to appeal against rejection without a separate procedural process. The Government said the reforms will reduce regulatory burden while protecting safeguards relating to public safety, fire and structural safety, environment, pollution control, labour safety, public health and land rights. The Bill seeks to advance the “Minimum Government, Maximum Facilitation” approach and strengthen Puducherry as a destination for investment, enterprise, innovation and employment.

The Garbhini Mitra Course About The Garbhini Mitra Course : What It Is? Garbhini Mitra is a structured, six-month offline healthcare skill-development training program. It blends traditional Ayurvedic maternal care principles with fundamental modern healthcare-support practices to develop non-clinical support personnel who provide lifestyle guidance, dietary advice, and wellness assistance to women throughout pregnancy and the postpartum period. Apex Implementing Body: All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi (an autonomous premier institution). Aim: To create a cadre of skilled community health workers and maternal wellness guides capable of delivering holistic, Ayurveda-based pre-conceptional, antenatal, and postnatal support to mothers and newborns, while facilitating timely clinical referrals to qualified medical professionals. Key Features of the Programme: Rooted in Classical Ayurvedic Frameworks: Built around three core traditional pillars: Garbhadhana Vidhi: Pre-conceptional health care and preparation. Garbhini Paricharya : Structured, month-by-month and trimester-specific antenatal regimen. Sutika Paricharya: Comprehensive postnatal care and maternal recovery practices. Trimester-Specific Wellness & Yoga : Trains participants in stage-specific dietary planning, pregnancy-safe yoga postures, breathing exercises, emotional support techniques during labor, and traditional newborn massage (Abhyanga). Basic Healthcare & Patient Safety Protocols: Incorporates essential modern non-clinical health practices, including Basic Life Support (BLS) , infection control, sanitization standards, workplace safety, and biomedical waste handling. Accessible Eligibility & Small Batch Size: Open to candidates who are at least 18 years of age and have completed the Senior Secondary (10+2) examination (with provision for students awaiting 12th-grade results); intake is capped at 20 students per batch to ensure focused practical training. Complementary Support & Early Warning Detection : Strictly designed to complement—not replace—clinical obstetrics; trained personnel assist mothers with routine health checks, track blood pressure/hemoglobin markers, identify high-risk warning signs, and facilitate prompt hospital referrals. national_raw_news.content: Parishrama Adalat resolves 65 delayed-payment cases worth ₹8.29 crore, helping MSEs restore cash flow, business continuity Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Parishrama Adalat resolves 65 delayed-payment cases worth ₹8.29 crore, helping MSEs restore cash flow, business continuity ANI | Updated: Aug 25, 2026 14:41 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 25 (ANI): The 'Parishrama Adalat', a Conciliation Conclave for Micro and Small Enterprise (MSE) delayed-payment disputes, organised by the Commissionerate of Industries and Commerce, Government of Telangana, in association with the Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME), successfully resolved 65 delayed-payment cases involving ₹8.29 crore. \Held at FTCCI, Hyderabad, the conclave brought together MSEs, buyers, public sector enterprises, MSE Facilitation Councils, ADR institutions and officials from the Ministry of MSME and the Government of Telangana. According to the press release by the Ministry of MSME, for an MSE, a delayed payment is not merely an unpaid invoice. It can affect salaries, purchase of raw materials, repayment of loans and the ability to take up new business opportunities. The Parishrama Adalat highlighted how timely and effective dispute resolution can support business continuity, restore confidence and strengthen commercial relationships. Shalini of Neemus Software Solutions Pvt. Ltd described prolonged delayed payments and contract-related disputes that had drained the enterprise's savings and confidence. Through the delayed-payment mechanism, the enterprise resolved nine out of eleven cases. Her experience highlighted the wider meaning of payment recovery--the restoration of confidence to continue operating and growing. Mukund Maheshwari of Nagarjuna Agro Chemicals Pvt Ltd shared how intervention by the Council helped clear an outstanding amount from a buyer who had earlier avoided his calls. Beyond recovery of the payment, the commercial relationship survived. He stated at the event, "Cash flow is the oxygen of industry." Atmakuri Nammalwar of Sree Solutions described waiting for more than two years for dues. Through the dispute-resolution mechanism, the enterprise reported recovery of close to ₹30 lakh, with four cases closed within approximately two to three months. A person with disability running a home-pipes business was able to pursue resolution of approximately ₹11 lakh in delayed payments. The case underscored the importance of ensuring that the circumstances of an entrepreneur do not become barriers to seeking a remedy. Through the ODR Platform, three conciliation meetings helped bring the parties together. One major buyer settled ₹20 lakh, while other buyers also began clearing their dues. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Finance RBI's USD-INR Swap Facility Sparks Unprecedented Forex Inflows into India, Banks Raise USD 73 Billion in eleven weeks Scheme’s Success Reflects Indian Diaspora’s confidence in India’s Banking sector and Economy Posted On: 24 AUG 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi The Reserve Bank of India's special USD-INR forex swap facility for FCNR(B) deposits, Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCB) and External Commercial Borrowings (ECB), launched on June 8, 2026, has driven an unprecedented surge in foreign exchange inflows into the country by mobilizing total foreign exchange inflows of US $73 billion as on August 21, 2026. FCNR(B) deposits alone accounted for US $65.40 billion, underlining the overwhelming response of Non-Resident Indians to the scheme. The scheme's success underscores the strength of the Indian diaspora, who have reposed faith in the Indian banking system and have once again demonstrated their enduring economic and emotional stake in India's growth story, channeling savings into FCNR(B) deposits at a pace that has consistently exceeded expectations. Having reached US$ 73 billion in under eleven weeks, with still another week to go, this stands out as the largest and fastest foreign-currency mobilisation exercises undertaken by India, comfortably surpassing the scale and pace of the RBI's 2013 FCNR(B) swap scheme, which had raised about US$ 26 billion over roughly three months. The response has been strong enough for the RBI to advance the closure of the FCNR(B) window itself, from September 30 to August 31, 2026, having already achieved its objective ahead of schedule. By securing large-scale, long-term non-resident deposits and commercial institutional funding entirely on tap, the Government of India has fortified its external buffers with maximum cost-efficiency.
